blocks.content: Avoiding exam traps is not just about knowledge, but about disciplined question reading and strategic time management under pressure.

rows: Underline or highlight negative qualifiers before reading options
Spending over 3 minutes on a single question
Use a two-pass approach: flag complex questions and move on
Recognize that extreme absolute statements in GS/Polity are usually false

items: Double-check questions asking for 'NOT CORRECT' options to prevent selecting the correct option by mistake.
Beware of distractors in options that represent common calculation errors made mid-way through a problem.
Treat extreme generalisations ('Always', 'Never', 'All') with caution in statement-based questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Negative marking severely penalizes blind guessing; prioritize logical elimination over random attempts.
Examiners frequently use qualifiers like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', 'ALWAYS', and 'ONLY' to create subtle traps.
Time-sink questions are intentionally placed to disrupt pacing—skip difficult items on your first pass.
Always verify units, signs (+/-), and decimal positions before selecting numerical options.
